summary: US-A2: A signed-in purchase belongs to the account
description:
**As** a signed-in buyer, **I want** my purchase attached to my account at the moment I make it,
**so that** I never have to quote an order reference to find it again.

**Priority:** P0  **Depends on:** TKT-220

This is the slice that makes an account worth having, and it is the one that touches the **checkout
path** - so it is also the slice where a mistake is expensive. The rule it must not break: a guest
checkout stays byte-for-byte what it is today.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `orders` gains a **nullable** customer reference. NULL means guest, guest stays the default,
  and nothing is backfilled. The column is nullable *because* the guest path is first-class, not as
  a migration convenience - say so in the migration comment.
- [ ] Checkout attributes the order to the authenticated customer. **The plan states how the caller
  proves it is that customer** and why that proof cannot be forged by a caller who simply names
  someone else's id. Attribution to a customer the caller has not authenticated as is **refused** -
  with a test that attempts exactly that.
- [ ] A **guest checkout is unchanged**: same request shape (no new required field), same response,
  same status codes, same recovery behaviour. A test pins that the guest path still stores NULL.
- [ ] The attribution does not perturb ADR-016's recovery states: `orders.status` gains no new value
  and `refunded` keeps meaning what it means (a compensated FAILED checkout).
- [ ] The order read exposes the attribution (contract-declared; regen committed).
- [ ] Replay/idempotency: re-submitting the same checkout with the same Idempotency-Key does not
  change or duplicate the attribution.
- [ ] Browser-submit verification (AGENTS.md): `make up`, then **submit** the new form(s) in a real browser — the smoke suite only renders, so the whole SSR-rejects-the-write class (origin check, base path, redirect, CSP) is invisible to it. Evidence in the PR. (buy while signed in, and buy while signed out.)
- [ ] `make check` green (lint + test + build, Go & TS, gateway smoke suite); regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) committed BEFORE the gate runs (ADR-009).

**Non-goals:** listing a customer's orders (TKT-222) - claiming a past guest order (TKT-223) -
purchase limits keyed on the customer (TKT-20) - transfers (TKT-9/TKT-160).

objective.note: An order made while signed in carries a stable customer identity; a guest order still carries none.

scope.note: One nullable column, one attribution path through checkout, one contract field. No read surface.

uncertainties.note: How the storefront proves the customer to commerce - session token exchanged for an assertion, a signed value, or a storefront-held credential. The ACs require the answer to be stated and to be unforgeable by a caller naming another id; the choice depends on TKT-220's ADR.

dependencies.note: Blocked by TKT-220 - there is no customer to attribute to until it lands.

approach.note: Follow the existing checkout write in services/commerce/internal/store/store.go, which already sets guest_order_ref under the same row lock. Attribution belongs in that same transaction, not a second write.

first_slice.note: Attributing at purchase time is strictly simpler than reconstructing attribution later, and TKT-222 has nothing to list without it.

success.note: Deterministic: signed-in checkout stores the customer, guest checkout stores NULL, a forged attribution is refused.

binding.rule: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code - floats are banned on money paths.

Local gate: `make check` (lint + test + build, Go & TS, plus the gateway smoke suite; run `make deps` first on a clean clone). CI runs the same gate - keep them mirrored. Commit regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) before running the gate - `check-generate` diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and fails the run.

A web-UI ticket isn't verified until a browser has *submitted* its forms. `make check`'s smoke suite exercises the catalog API directly and only *renders* back-office pages - it never submits an Astro form, so the whole class of "the SSR layer rejects/mangles the request before the handler runs" (CSRF/`checkOrigin`, base-path rewrites, redirects, CSP) is invisible to it.

governingAdrs.why: Cuts the system at five services + a stateless gateway. Customer accounts must land inside an existing service or the deviation is recorded as an ADR - ADR-042 rejected a sixth identity service and rejected giving the gateway a database.

The precedent AND its reasoning: staff accounts in catalog because catalog owns organizers; the SSR app owns the session, not the service; sessions in-process and unpersisted; per-principal session cap is what bounds the map; the cookie is path-scoped because storefront/scanner/admin/api share ONE origin. It also records that Astro's `security.checkOrigin` CANNOT be turned on behind the gateway (the Node adapter compares against the container Host) - a proxy-aware origin check replaces it.

The rule for where a guard lives: declared `security:` guards operations in a service's PUBLIC contract; an inline `X-Internal-Token` check guards its INTERNAL surface. Commerce's 404-on-internal is load-bearing (it matches the gateway edge-deny), not cargo. Whichever surface customer register/authenticate lands on, this decides how it is guarded.
Contract-first: any new operation is declared in the service's openapi.yaml and the generated code is committed before the gate runs.
Migrations run OUT-OF-BAND - the binary's `migrate` subcommand as a one-shot Compose job the service waits on. The server path never migrates. Any new table follows this.

The checkout recovery state machine. `orders.status='refunded'` already means a compensated FAILED checkout - do not overload order status. Anything added to the checkout path must not perturb the recovery states.

`guest_order_ref` is a BEARER credential for the ticket bundle (`/api/access/orders/{ref}/tickets` needs nothing else) and is never logged - TKT-202 is an open bug where the gateway logs it. Anything that surfaces or accepts an order ref inherits both properties.

Name the adversary before claiming a security property. 'A customer cannot see another customer's orders' means an unauthenticated or differently-authenticated HTTP caller - it says nothing about anyone with database access.
Response drift fails closed: a handler whose response does not match the declared schema is refused, so a new operation's schema must actually match what the handler writes.

reference.summary: BLAST RADIUS - `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN` (compose.yaml `&go-env` anchor) is ONE shared value across all five Go services: whatever holds it can call commerce's /internal/orders/{id}/refunds, inventory's /internal/operational-holds and /internal/slots/{id}/capacity-adjustments, and access's refund surface. The storefront must NEVER receive it.
BLAST RADIUS - `COMMERCE_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN` opens commerce's staff refund (money-moving). Held today only by the back office. The storefront must NEVER receive it.

The storefront container today has exactly ONE env var: `GATEWAY_URL`. It holds no credential of any kind and serves anonymous internet traffic. Any design that hands it a token is a new trust decision that must be argued, not assumed.

Precedent to mirror, not to copy blindly: staff sign-in is catalog `staff_accounts` (migration 0015, bcrypt + tripwire CHECK + non-empty-Down refusal), `services/catalog/internal/store/staff.go`, `services/catalog/internal/api/staff.go`; the SESSION lives in the back-office Astro process (`web/backoffice/src/lib/session.ts`, `gate.ts`, `src/middleware.ts`) - opaque 256-bit token, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, absolute 8h TTL, per-principal cap of 5, cookie scoped to `/admin` NOT `/`.

The checkout write that already exists and that this ticket extends: `services/commerce/internal/store/store.go` sets `orders.status='completed'` and mints `guest_order_ref` under a `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the order row. Attribution goes in that transaction.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — TKT-221

**Branch:** `TKT-221-order-attribution` off `origin/main` @ `c3d11f84` (TKT-220 merged as `3f215d69`).
**Routing (config.models):** plan = `gpt-5.6-luna` · planReview = `main-agent` · implement =
`main-agent` · aiReview = `gpt-5.6-luna`. Cross-model invariant checked both ways. No substitution.

**Blockers:** TKT-220 — **resolved** (merged, Done). Zero open blockers.

**Selection reason:** the only claimable child of TKT-21. TKT-222 is blocked by this ticket and
TKT-223 by TKT-222, so there is no choice to make.

**Gate waiver:** the same owner waiver recorded in full on TKT-220 applies to this run — all four
human gates replaced by agent judgement, everything else in the skill unchanged. The `overrides:`
list in this ticket's closeout is the audit record for it.

### Risk verdict: **`risk:low` NOT claimed**

Stated explicitly even though it is obvious (TKT-190's lesson: the carve-outs are exactly the tickets
whose risk is obvious to the claimer and invisible in the thread afterwards). This one hits:

1. **A data migration** — a new column on `orders`, the table the checkout path writes under a row
   lock.
2. **The money path** — attribution happens during checkout. Nothing about the amounts changes, but
   the code that changes is the code that completes a paid order.
3. **Auth** — "the caller cannot attribute an order to a customer they have not authenticated as" is
   an authentication claim, and proving it is most of this ticket.
4. Likely **>5 files**.

The owner's stop conditions name auth, money paths and data migrations. All three are **anticipated
by the ticket** — they are the ticket — so this proceeds under the waiver. Flagged so every
downstream reader applies the right lens.

### Context-mémo re-resolved at claim

Re-resolved against `docs/adr/` at HEAD rather than trusted from shaping. **One ADR has landed since
the bake and it is the most important one here: [ADR-049](docs/adr/ADR-049-customer-identity-and-storefront-sessions.md)**
(TKT-220) — customer identity lives in commerce, the storefront owns an in-process session, and the
storefront holds **no service credential**. That last point is the constraint this ticket runs into
head-first: the storefront knows who the customer is and commerce does not, and the obvious fix
(hand the storefront a token, or let it name a `customer_id` in the checkout body) is either the
trust boundary ADR-049 §1 refused or a forgery anyone can perform against the public gateway.

Governing set: **ADR-049** (above), **ADR-016** (checkout recovery states — `orders.status='refunded'`
already means a compensated FAILED checkout; do not overload it), **ADR-002**, **ADR-009**,
**ADR-022**, **ADR-043**, **ADR-021** (name the adversary), **ADR-028** (response drift fails
closed), **ADR-012** (`guest_order_ref` is a bearer credential, never logged).

Credential blast radius, unchanged and re-stated because this ticket will be tempted:
`INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN` is one shared value opening every service's internal surface;
`COMMERCE_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN` opens a money-moving refund; the storefront holds **only**
`GATEWAY_URL`. Neither may reach it.

**Schema trap carried forward from the last ticket:** commerce's `Checkout` schema is
`additionalProperties: false` with four required fields, and `ReservationCreate` next to it uses
`minProperties`/`maxProperties`/`not` to express an XOR — a new optional field on the wrong schema
silently breaks a constraint that is doing real work. Check which schema is being extended.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Execution plan — draft

**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-luna`** (config.models.plan) via the codex companion, read-only, effort=high.
Job `task-mshxkw76-rfe0ef`, model confirmed in the job state file — no substitution.

The brief handed it the ticket + ACs verbatim, the governing ADRs (including ADR-049, one hour old),
the AGENTS.md binding rules, the credential blast radii, a read-list, and one framed hard problem:
**the storefront knows who the customer is and commerce does not.** It was told the two obvious
answers are wrong and asked to say why.

---

# 1. Decision summary

Choose a commerce-minted, signed customer assertion carried in an optional `X-Customer-Assertion` header.

Commerce signs `customer_id` plus an absolute expiry using a new, commerce-only HMAC key. `registerCustomer` and `authenticateCustomer` include the assertion in the existing `CustomerPrincipal` response. The storefront stores it beside the existing in-process session entry; it is never placed in the `sf_sid` cookie, browser storage, or checkout body.

Because `HoldPicker` is a browser-side island and `sf_sid` is `httpOnly`, checkout must pass through a new storefront server endpoint. That endpoint reads the existing session, forwards the unchanged body and `Idempotency-Key` to `/api/commerce/orders`, and adds the assertion only for a live signed-in session. The gateway remains unchanged: `/api/checkout` already falls through its existing `/` storefront route, while `/api/commerce/` remains the direct commerce route.

The assertion is verified before `claimOrder` performs any order, payment, or inventory work. An internet caller who can POST directly through the gateway but does not possess a valid assertion or the commerce signing key cannot attribute an order to an arbitrary customer. Adding `customer_id` to the JSON body remains forbidden by `Checkout.additionalProperties: false`; a tampered assertion whose customer id is changed without recomputing the signature returns 401. A caller with their own valid assertion can attribute only to their own account. A stolen valid assertion remains a bearer credential until expiry; this plan does not claim protection against that adversary, nor against a process/database administrator who can read or alter service state (ADR-021).

A dedicated `COMMERCE_CUSTOMER_ASSERTION_KEY` is required. It must not reuse `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN` or `COMMERCE_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN`. Reusing either would broaden a customer checkout proof into access to unrelated internal operations or money-moving refunds.

Rejected alternatives:

- A body `customer_id` is forgeable by any public caller and is rejected by the contract.
- A storefront service credential violates ADR-049 §1 and places a powerful credential in a process serving anonymous traffic.
- A persisted commerce session/reference table contradicts ADR-049 §4, duplicates the storefront session lifecycle, and creates restart, expiry, revocation, and cleanup work.
- Re-authentication at checkout exposes the password to another money-path request and is unacceptable UX.
- A storefront proxy alone is not an identity proof; without either a signed assertion, persisted reference, or service credential, commerce still cannot distinguish it from an attacker.

A stale/expired session is refused by the storefront checkout endpoint with 401 before commerce is called. The buyer must sign in again and retry using the same idempotency key; an already-created order retains its original attribution. A direct commerce request with an expired assertion also returns 401 before side effects. Signed-out checkout continues through the proxy without an assertion and remains guest checkout.

Create migration `0016` with nullable `orders.customer_id REFERENCES customer_accounts(id)`. The migration comment must say explicitly that NULL means guest, guest checkout is first-class, and the column is nullable for that domain reason—not as a migration convenience. The migration only adds the column; existing orders remain NULL and are not backfilled.

`claimOrder` must capture the verified customer id on the initial order row so recovery can finish the order after the assertion/session expires. The value is immutable for the idempotency record: replay cannot replace a customer id with another id or turn a guest order into an attributed order. `CompleteOrder` must read the value under its existing `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` and keep completion, `guest_order_ref`, `customer_id`, and the completion outbox in the same transaction; no post-completion attribution write is allowed.

The checkout response remains unchanged, including `guest_order_ref`. `OrderState` gains a required nullable `customer_id`, so `GET /orders/{id}` returns either the attributed UUID or JSON `null`.

# 2. ADR

Amend `docs/adr/ADR-049-customer-identity-and-storefront-sessions.md`; do not create a separate ADR. This is an extension of the exact identity/session boundary ADR-049 already established.

Add a section covering:

- commerce-signed, expiring checkout assertions;
- the dedicated commerce-only signing key and its Compose/bootstrap wiring;
- the storefront server-side checkout bridge required by browser-side islands and `httpOnly` sessions;
- optional proof semantics preserving guest checkout;
- proof expiry and re-authentication/replay behavior;
- immutable attribution under idempotency and recovery;
- bearer-token limitations and the explicit ADR-021 adversary boundary;
- no change to the ADR-016 status vocabulary or completion event payload.

# 3. Definition of Done

1. `orders.customer_id` is nullable, NULL means guest, no rows are backfilled, and the migration comment explains that nullability is required because guest checkout is first-class.

2. Checkout verifies a commerce-signed assertion, persists only the authenticated customer, refuses a tampered/arbitrary customer attribution, and has a test attempting exactly that forgery.

3. Guest checkout keeps the current request body, response body, status codes, and recovery behavior; a test proves the guest order stores `customer_id IS NULL`.

4. No `orders.status` value changes; `refunded` remains a compensated FAILED checkout, and recovery preserves attribution independently of status.

5. `GET /orders/{id}` declares and returns nullable `customer_id`; generated Go and TypeScript contract files are regenerated and committed.

6. Repeating the same checkout with the same `Idempotency-Key` neither duplicates nor changes `customer_id`, including guest-first and attributed-first replays.

7. With `make up` running, a real browser submits checkout once signed out and once signed in; both paths are verified through the storefront, not only through direct API calls.

8. Generated files are committed before `make check` runs, and `make check` completes successfully.

# 4. Files

### Commerce schema and contract

- Create `services/commerce/internal/store/migrations/0016_order_customer_attribution.sql` with the nullable foreign key and no-backfill comment.
- Modify `services/commerce/api/openapi.yaml` to add `customer_assertion` to `CustomerPrincipal`, declare the optional checkout assertion header and 401 response, and add required nullable `customer_id` to `OrderState`.
- Regenerate and commit `services/commerce/internal/api/openapi_gen.go`.
- Regenerate and commit `web/storefront/src/lib/commerce-api-types.gen.ts`.

### Commerce runtime

- Modify `services/commerce/internal/api/customer.go` to mint assertions in `principalResponse`.
- Modify `services/commerce/internal/api/server.go` to verify the assertion before `claimOrder`, freeze attribution during idempotent order claiming, and expose `customer_id` from `getOrder`.
- Modify `services/commerce/internal/store/store.go` so `Completion`/`CompleteOrder` carry and lock attribution with completion and outbox work.
- Modify `services/commerce/internal/store/recovery.go` so `StuckOrder` and `Completion()` preserve `customer_id`.
- Modify `services/commerce/cmd/commerce/main.go` to require and inject the dedicated assertion key.
- Modify `compose.yaml` to provide `COMMERCE_CUSTOMER_ASSERTION_KEY` only to commerce.
- Modify `Makefile` `env-bootstrap` to generate the dedicated key independently.
- Modify `scripts/smoke.sh` to generate and export an isolated assertion key for smoke runs.

### Storefront

- Modify `web/storefront/src/lib/customer-api.ts` to consume `customer_assertion`.
- Modify `web/storefront/src/lib/session.ts` to store the assertion server-side beside the principal while keeping `sf_sid` opaque and `httpOnly`.
- Modify `web/storefront/src/pages/[locale]/account/sign-in.astro` and `register.astro` to place the returned assertion into the in-process session.
- Create `web/storefront/src/pages/api/checkout.ts` as the server-side checkout proxy.
- Modify `web/storefront/src/components/HoldPicker.tsx` to call `/api/checkout` and reuse one `Idempotency-Key` across retries for the reservation.

### Tests

- Extend `services/commerce/internal/api/customer_test.go`.
- Extend `services/commerce/internal/api/server_test.go`.
- Extend `services/commerce/internal/store/customer_test.go`.
- Extend `services/commerce/internal/store/migration_smoke_test.go`.
- Extend `services/commerce/internal/store/completion_smoke_test.go`.
- Extend `services/commerce/internal/store/recovery_smoke_test.go`.
- Extend `services/commerce/internal/recovery/runner_test.go`.
- Extend `smoke/checkout_test.go` and `smoke/customer_accounts_test.go`.
- Extend `web/storefront/test/session.test.ts` and `web/storefront/test/hold-picker.test.ts`.
- Create `web/storefront/test/checkout.test.ts` for proxy forwarding, expiry, and response preservation.

# 5. Test plan

### Commerce assertion and handler seam

First failing assertions:

- A valid authenticated principal contains a non-empty assertion whose verified customer id equals the authenticated account.
- Changing only the customer id or expiry bytes makes verification fail.
- An expired assertion returns 401 before `claimOrder` is called.
- Adding `customer_id` to the checkout body returns 400 from the contract validator.
- A valid assertion for customer A modified to name customer B returns 401; no order is created for B.
- The assertion and password never appear in handler responses or logs.

### Store and migration seam

First failing assertions:

- Upgrading a schema containing pre-existing orders leaves every existing `customer_id` NULL.
- A newly inserted guest order has NULL attribution.
- A known customer UUID is accepted; an unknown UUID fails the foreign key.
- `CompleteOrder` preserves the locked customer id, returns one canonical guest reference under concurrent completion, and owes one outbox event.
- A replay with a different customer assertion cannot replace the stored attribution.
- `ClaimStuckOrders` reads attribution and `StuckOrder.Completion()` passes it through recovery completion.

### Recovery seam

First failing assertions:

- Recovery completion of an attributed `created` or `confirmation_pending` order retains its customer id.
- `declined`, `timeout`, `reconciliation_required`, and `refunded` retain their existing meanings.
- `refunded` remains terminal compensation and never becomes a new attribution/status state.
- Existing `TestClassifyRecoveredCoversTheStatusVocabulary` still covers exactly the unchanged vocabulary.
- Existing `TestRefundLeavesCheckoutStatusCompleted` still proves refund state is separate from checkout status.

### Idempotency and smoke seam

First failing assertions:

- Signed-in checkout followed by the same key/body/proof returns the same order and customer id.
- Guest checkout followed by the same key with a signed-in proof remains guest and does not mutate attribution.
- Two concurrent requests with the same key produce one order and one attribution.
- Direct gateway checkout with no assertion remains guest.
- Direct gateway checkout with a valid assertion attributes the order and `GET /orders/{id}` returns that UUID.

### Storefront seam

First failing assertions:

- Signed-out `/api/checkout` forwards the exact body, status, response bytes, and idempotency key without an assertion.
- Signed-in `/api/checkout` forwards the exact body and adds only the assertion header; it never forwards `sf_sid`.
- An expired session returns 401 without calling commerce.
- The cookie remains opaque, `httpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, and `Path=/`.
- `HoldPicker` retries with the same idempotency key after an expiry/authentication interruption.

### Browser-submit verification

Run `make up`, then use a real browser against the gateway:

- Signed out: reserve, submit the existing checkout form, verify the unchanged completed response/ticket link and `customer_id: null`.
- Signed in: register or sign in through the real Astro form, submit the same checkout form, then read the order through the commerce API and verify the returned `customer_id` matches the signed-in principal.
- Repeat the signed-in submission with the same key and verify no duplicate order or attribution change.

Only after generated files are committed, run `make check`.

# 6. Risks and traps

- Do not put the assertion in the checkout body; `Checkout` is closed and guest checkout has no new required field.
- Do not put the assertion in `sf_sid`, local storage, or a browser-readable cookie.
- Do not route `/api/checkout` through commerce; the existing gateway `/` catch-all must reach the storefront proxy.
- Do not reuse either existing service credential.
- Do not include the assertion in the idempotency fingerprint; expiry changes must not turn a legitimate replay into a conflict.
- Do not let a later proof replace an attribution already frozen by the first idempotent order claim.
- Persist attribution before payment can become recoverable; otherwise ADR-016 recovery cannot know the customer after the original session expires.
- Keep `buyer_pii` as the order-time snapshot; it is not the account identity.
- Keep `guest_order_ref` out of logs per ADR-012, and never log assertion headers.
- Declare the new 401 response and nullable `OrderState.customer_id` before implementation; ADR-028 will otherwise turn valid behavior into a contract 500.
- Run migration through the existing commerce `migrate` subcommand and `commerce-migrate` Compose dependency; never add server-path migration logic.
- Do not change the completion event payload merely to carry attribution; that would invoke ADR-017 without a consumer need.
- Regeneration before committing is mandatory; running `make check` with generated drift will fail even if the implementation is correct.
- Browser submission is mandatory because the existing smoke suite does not exercise Astro form/proxy behavior.

# 7. What this constrains downstream

TKT-222 must treat `orders.customer_id` as the ownership dimension and add an indexed, authenticated customer-order read path; the public `GET /orders/{id}` response is informational, not an authorization check. TKT-223 must keep `guest_order_ref` as its separate bearer credential and perform claiming atomically without confusing a guest order’s NULL `customer_id` with an unverified customer assertion. Changing the assertion format, expiry, session storage, or attribution immutability after either ticket ships would require coordinated wallet/claim semantics and potentially a data migration, so those rules belong in the ADR-049 amendment now.

# 8. Follow-up tickets to file

- Customer assertion key rotation, revocation, and multi-key verification.
- Multi-replica/session-store support if storefront scaling becomes required.
- TKT-222 customer-order listing with indexed ownership authorization.
- TKT-223 guest-order claiming and its concurrency/idempotency rules.
- TKT-224 rate limiting for registration, authentication, assertion failures, and checkout abuse.
- Review whether public order reads should expose customer UUIDs or require an ownership-aware read contract.

<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=summary -->
### Adversarial plan critique — by `main-agent` (config.models.planReview)

Cross-model invariant held: the draft is `gpt-5.6-luna`'s. Every file, symbol and seam it names was
checked against **HEAD**.

#### Existence check — all verified present

`claimOrder` (`server.go`) · `StuckOrder` (`server.go`, `internal/recovery/clients.go`) ·
`Completion()` (`store/recovery.go`) · `TestClassifyRecoveredCoversTheStatusVocabulary`
(`api/server_test.go`) · `TestRefundLeavesCheckoutStatusCompleted` (`store/refunds_smoke_test.go`) ·
`env-bootstrap` (Makefile) · `internal/recovery/runner_test.go` · `web/storefront/test/hold-picker.test.ts` ·
`completion_smoke_test.go` · `recovery_smoke_test.go`. Commerce migrations stop at `0015`, so `0016`
is next. **No hallucinated seams.**

The draft found the two facts that decide this ticket, and it found them by reading rather than
assuming: `HoldPicker` is a `client:load` island that fetches `/api/commerce/orders` **from the
browser**, so the storefront SSR process is not in the checkout path at all; and `sf_sid` is
`httpOnly`, so the island cannot read it. Those two together are why a proxy is unavoidable, and the
draft is right that a proxy *alone* is not an identity proof. Accepted as the shape of the solution.

---

### Findings

#### F1 — [blocking] The assertion's lifetime is not tied to the session's, and the failure lands on the payment button

The plan gives the assertion "an absolute expiry" and never says what it is relative to
`SESSION_TTL_MS` (8h). If the assertion is shorter, this is the sequence:

1. Buyer signs in. Storefront session: 8h. Assertion: shorter.
2. Buyer browses, picks seats, **holds inventory on a short TTL**, fills in payment.
3. Assertion has expired. The proxy 401s, or commerce does.
4. There is **no re-mint path**: the storefront holds the principal, not the password. The only
   recovery is signing in again — and the hold is expiring while they do it.

So a shorter assertion converts a silent background expiry into a failure at the single worst moment
in the flow, on the money path, for a buyer who did nothing wrong.

**Amendment:** the assertion expires **exactly when the session does** — same TTL, anchored at the
same instant, minted in the same operation. Then "the session is alive" and "the assertion is valid"
are one statement rather than two that can disagree, and the whole class of mid-checkout expiry
disappears. It costs nothing in exposure: the assertion lives only inside the storefront's in-process
session, so it is already unreachable once that session is gone. The ADR amendment must state that
the two lifetimes are deliberately coupled, or a later "tighten the token" change reintroduces this.

#### F2 — [blocking] The new key must join commerce's existing startup separation check

`services/commerce/cmd/commerce/main.go:111-127` already refuses to start when
`COMMERCE_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN` equals `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN`, with a comment explaining that the
separate credential exists precisely so one leaking does not imply the other. `scripts/smoke.sh`
generates all three from independent `/dev/urandom` reads for the same reason, and says so.

The plan adds a **third** credential and wires it through `main.go`, `compose.yaml`, `env-bootstrap`
and `smoke.sh` — but never mentions the separation check. A third credential that is not in it is the
one credential whose separation is never verified, and identical values look configured.

**Amendment:** `COMMERCE_CUSTOMER_ASSERTION_KEY` joins the startup check against **both** existing
credentials, and `smoke.sh` generates it from its own `/dev/urandom` read. A test asserts the refusal
— the check is worthless if nothing proves it fires.

#### F3 — [blocking] Do not change `HoldPicker`'s idempotency-key generation

The plan proposes "reuse one `Idempotency-Key` across retries for the reservation". Today it is
`crypto.randomUUID()` per click (`HoldPicker.tsx:112`).

That is a behaviour change to **checkout idempotency**, on the money path, that this ticket did not
ask for. Its failure modes are not small: a reused key with a changed body is a fingerprint mismatch
(409 conflict on a legitimate retry), and a reused key that *matches* silently collapses a genuine
second attempt into a replay of the first. Either is a money-path defect introduced as a
convenience.

**Amendment:** leave it exactly as it is. If there is a real defect in per-click key generation, it
is a finding to file, not a change to smuggle into an attribution ticket.

#### F4 — [blocking, and it is the one that breaks everything if wrong] Routing checkout through the storefront puts the origin check in front of it — **including for guests**

The plan sends **both** guest and signed-in checkout through the new proxy. That means checkout now
passes `gateRequest` (`web/storefront/src/lib/gate.ts`), which refuses **every unsafe method** whose
`Origin` does not match the public origin the gateway reports — and refuses outright when `Origin` is
absent.

The existing checkout is a **`fetch` from a React island**, not a form submission. If that fetch does
not carry an `Origin` the gate trusts, **guest checkout breaks for everyone**, and it breaks in the
one layer `make check` cannot see (the smoke suite drives the commerce API directly; it has never
traversed the storefront SSR for a checkout).

This is the same class of failure as TKT-105 and as TKT-220's `checkOrigin` default — an SSR layer
refusing a write before the handler runs — and this ticket walks a *working, money-carrying* path
into it.

**Amendment:** the DoD gains an explicit, named item: **the browser check must submit a real guest
checkout through the proxy and see it complete**, before anything else is claimed. And the proxy must
forward commerce's status code and response **bytes** unchanged, so "guest checkout is unchanged"
means the observable response, not just the request shape.

I considered requiring guest checkout to keep posting directly to `/api/commerce/orders` and routing
only signed-in checkout through the proxy. Rejected: the island cannot tell whether it is signed in
(the cookie is `httpOnly` and the event page never resolves the session), so it would need a new
SSR-passed flag and two code paths through the money path — more risk than the one it removes, and
the single path is provable in a browser in one run.

#### F5 — [non-blocking] `/api/checkout` is the wrong path

It works: the gateway's route table has no bare `/api/` entry, so `/api/checkout` falls through to
the `/` storefront catch-all (verified in `gateway/cmd/gateway/main.go`). But in this system
`/api/<svc>/` means *"the gateway proxies this to a service"*, and a storefront-served route inside
that namespace reads as a service call to anyone debugging the route table — while depending on a
fallthrough rather than a registration.

**Amendment:** serve it at **`/checkout`**. Same catch-all, none of the ambiguity, and no chance a
future `/api/` entry shadows it.

#### F6 — [non-blocking] A bearer credential now lives in a public contract response

`customer_assertion` is added to `CustomerPrincipal`, which is the response body of two **public**
operations. That is correct — the caller has just proven the password — but it means the contract now
declares a field that is a bearer credential for the account until expiry.

**Amendment:** say it in the ADR amendment in those words, and pin two things: `customer-api.ts` must
never log the response, and the storefront must never place the assertion anywhere the browser can
reach (not the cookie, not a prop, not `locals` that a page renders). The draft says this for the
storefront; the contract side is unstated.

#### F7 — [non-blocking, accepted] Sizing

19 runtime/config files plus 11 test files is at the top of "one reviewable PR". It is not splittable
without leaving a non-demoable half — a column nothing writes, or an assertion nothing consumes.
Noted rather than acted on, and the reviewer of the diff should know it was a deliberate call.

---

### Pre-mortem

1. **Most likely: guest checkout 403s in the browser** and the gate is not the first place anyone
   looks, because the change was "about attribution". F4 exists to make this the first thing checked.
2. **Second: a buyer is 401'd at the payment button** because the assertion outlived its usefulness
   before the session did. F1.
3. **Third: recovery completes an order and loses the attribution**, because the customer id was read
   from a request that no longer exists. The draft already caught this — attribution must be captured
   on the initial `claimOrder` row and re-read under `CompleteOrder`'s existing `FOR UPDATE`, never
   passed forward from the handler.
4. **Fourth: the idempotency fingerprint includes the assertion**, so a legitimate retry after a
   re-sign-in becomes a 409. The draft names it; it belongs in the DoD, not only the risk list.
5. **Fifth, quiet and expensive: the third credential is generated as a copy of another** in one of
   the four places it must be wired, and every test still passes. F2.

### Verdict

**Accept with amendments.** The draft solves the hard problem correctly and its adversary analysis is
honest about what a stolen assertion buys. Four blocking findings, all fixable inside the plan; none
requires re-drafting.

### Decisions made by the agent in place of Gate 2

**D1 — Single checkout path through the proxy, for guests too (F4).** The critique recommends it and
explains the rejected alternative: the island cannot tell whether it is signed in, so a two-path
design needs an SSR-passed flag and two code paths through the money path. One path, proven in a
browser. *Reversibility:* the island's fetch URL is one string.

**D2 — Assertion TTL = session TTL (A1), rather than a shorter "safer" number.** The critique
recommends it. The apparent safety of a shorter token is illusory here: it lives only inside the
in-process session, so it is already unreachable the moment that session is gone, and a shorter one
buys nothing except a 401 on the payment button.

**D3 — Amend ADR-049 rather than write ADR-050.** From the draft, unchallenged by the critique. This
extends the identity/session boundary ADR-049 established; a second ADR would split one decision
across two documents. *Reversibility:* an amendment can be promoted to its own ADR later; splitting a
decision is harder to undo than joining it.

**D4 — Assertion format: HMAC-SHA256 over `customer_id|expiry`, base64url, verified in constant
time.** Neither draft nor critique specified the primitive. Most reversible and least novel: the
repo already uses `crypto/subtle` constant-time comparison for credentials
(`catalog/internal/api/write_credential.go`), `crypto/hmac` is stdlib, and nothing here needs a JWT's
generality — no third party parses this token, and a format nobody else reads is a format we can
change without coordination.

**D5 — On assertion-verification failure, commerce answers 401 and creates nothing.** From the draft.
Explicitly *not* "fall back to a guest order": silently downgrading a signed-in purchase to a guest
one would make an attribution failure invisible to the buyer, who would then not find the order in
the wallet TKT-222 builds, with no error anywhere.

Four reached the (waived) gate reviewed by nobody but their author:

1. **The assertion/session lifetime coupling (A1/D2)** — the largest, and it changes a security

2. **The startup separation check extension (A2)** — a change to a fail-closed startup path.
3. **Refusing the idempotency-key change (A3)** — a *removal* from the plan, which no code review

4. **The `/checkout` path (A5)** and the guest-through-proxy browser requirement (A4).

### The plan simplified itself once the code was read

The draft required `CompleteOrder` to "read the value under its existing `FOR UPDATE` and keep
completion, `guest_order_ref`, `customer_id` and the outbox in the same transaction", and
`recovery.go` to thread attribution through `StuckOrder`/`Completion()`.

**None of that was needed.** `CompleteOrder` only ever `UPDATE`s `status` and `guest_order_ref`, so
an attribution written at `claimOrder` survives completion — and recovery — **by not being touched**.
The simplest correct change was no change at all in either file. What replaced the code is a test
that pins the property (`TestCompletionLeavesAttributionUntouched`), because "it survives because
nothing writes it" is exactly the kind of thing a later edit breaks silently.

One thing the plan did **not** anticipate and the code did: `exchanges.go` has the only other
production `INSERT INTO orders`. Without inheriting `customer_id`, a signed-in buyer's *exchanged*
order would silently disappear from their account — indistinguishable, from their side, from a lost
order. It now copies the source's attribution inside the INSERT.

### Mutation checks

| Mutation | Test that caught it |
|---|---|
| MAC covers only the customer id, not the expiry | `TestCustomerAssertionRoundTrips` + `…Expires` |
| Expiry parsed but never enforced | `TestCustomerAssertionExpires` |
| Bridge drops the assertion header | bridge: attaches for a live session |
| Bridge forwards the cookie | bridge: never the cookie — **after the fixture was fixed** |
| Separation check loses the two new pairs | `TestCredentialsAreDistinctRefusesEveryCollidingPair` |

**One blind fixture, caught by the mutation check.** The bridge test set the session cookie only via
the `cookies` accessor, never as a `Cookie` **header** on the request — so adding `cookie` to the
forwarding allowlist left the suite green. A real browser sends the header; the fixture did not. Now
it does, and the mutation fails as it should. Third ticket running, third fixture that could not show
the negative it was written for.

### The gate failed once

Two smoke tests (`TestCommerceStartsWithoutRunningBackfill`,
`TestCommerceBackfillRepairsSeededOrder`) build a commerce container **by hand** rather than through
compose, so they carry their own env list — and commerce's new fail-fast on
`COMMERCE_CUSTOMER_ASSERTION_KEY` was doing exactly its job. The env list in those probes is
hand-maintained, which is the shape of thing that goes stale; it went stale within an hour of the
credential existing.

### Browser verification — 9 checks, real Google Chrome

The one that mattered: **routing checkout through the storefront puts the origin check in front of
it, for guests too.** A previously direct, money-carrying path now traverses the layer that TKT-105
and TKT-220 both got caught by, and `make check` cannot see it.

- the island posts to `/checkout`, not straight to commerce
- **a real browser does send `Origin` on the island's `fetch`** — the gate depends on it
- **a GUEST completes checkout through the bridge**: 200, guest order ref, `customer_id: null`
- a signed-in buyer's purchase comes back **attributed**
- the assertion never reaches the browser

*A note on that Origin check, because it nearly produced a false alarm:* Playwright's
`request.headers()` omits headers the browser adds at the network layer, so it reported no `Origin`
on a request the server had demonstrably accepted. `allHeaders()` is the accurate one. A probe that
disagrees with an observed 200 is the probe being wrong.

Driving the browser also needed a **seeded on-sale performance** — a fresh stack has none, and the
smoke suite's fixtures live inside its own test run. Seeded through the same public catalog contract
the smoke suite uses.

Each pass got the **diff only**, primed for guilt. Pass 2 reviewed **only the fix diff**.

### Pass 1 — five findings, all confirmed

| # | Finding | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| F1 [high] | Key rotation → 401 rendered as payment uncertainty | **Fixed** |
| F2 [medium] | Session expiry not actually synchronized with the assertion's | **Fixed** |
| F3 [medium] | Bridge has no timeout or network-failure path | **Fixed** |
| F4 [medium] | Attribution durability tests never drive recovery or exchange writes | **Fixed** |
| F5 [medium] | Bridge tests cannot detect assertion-header smuggling | **Fixed** |

**F1 is the one that mattered.** `HoldPicker` handled 402 and 408 and nothing else, so a 401 —
raised *before any order exists*, no money moved — fell through to "payment status is being checked".
A lie in the frightening direction.

**F2 was a gap between the design and the code.** Equal TTLs are not synchronized lifetimes: commerce
mints at T1 on its clock, the storefront starts the session at T2 on its own, so the session outlived
the assertion by a round trip. Near the boundary that is precisely the 401-at-the-payment-button the
equal TTLs were chosen to prevent.

**F5 was a fixture that could not fail** — the third on this run. The bridge test never sent an
inbound `X-Customer-Assertion`, so adding it to the forwarding allowlist left the suite green, and
any internet caller could have attributed a purchase to any customer.

### Pass 2 — six findings; two [high], both about what pass 1's fixes *claimed*

| # | Finding | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| S1 [high] | 503 described as retry-safe after commerce may have accepted payment | **Fixed** |
| S2 [high] | 401 does not prove no order exists | **Fixed** |
| S3 [medium] | Cap is not correct under clock skew; `Number` parses non-canonical values | **Fixed** |
| S4 [medium] | Source scanner misses `UPDATE orders o SET` and other real shapes | **Fixed** |
| S5 [medium] | Timeout test cannot see the timeout | **Fixed** |
| S6 [medium] | `request.text()` is outside the deadline | **Answered, not fixed** |

**S1 and S2 are the useful kind of finding: both fixes were correct and both said something false
about themselves.**

- The bridge's 503 comment said "nothing was submitted, so a retry is safe". A disconnect can land
  *after* payments accepted the charge; only the response was lost. It now says the outcome is
  **unknown**, which drops the island into the same branch it used before this bridge existed. Worth
  recording what actually protects the buyer: commerce, not the bridge — a retry carries a fresh
  Idempotency-Key while an order already exists for that reservation, and `claimOrder` answers
  `errCheckoutConflict` rather than charging again.
- The 401 copy said "your seats are still held". Commerce verifies the assertion **before** resolving
  an existing order, so a retry of an already-successful checkout whose assertion has since died gets
  the same 401 — order completed, seats confirmed. The copy now points at the tickets page instead of
  asserting a state the client cannot see.

**S4 found the detector could not detect.** `recovery.go` already writes `UPDATE orders o SET`, and
the patterns required `orders` to be followed immediately by `SET`. A scanner that silently skips a
real statement is worse than none, so aliases are handled and a test now asserts the scanner **sees**
each shape it must recognise. Its real limit is stated rather than implied — it reads Go source, so
runtime-assembled SQL defeats it, and a test checks nothing in this service does that.

**S6 answered, not fixed:** `await request.text()` runs before `fetch`, so `AbortSignal.timeout`
cannot bound it. True. An end-to-end SSR request deadline belongs to the adapter, not to one route,
and building a per-route one to close a case the Node server already bounds would be scope this
ticket did not ask for. Recorded here rather than silently left.

### Every fix test was mutation-checked

12 mutations across both rounds, 12 caught: MAC not covering the expiry · expiry unenforced ·
attribution dropped from the bridge · cookie forwarded · caller-supplied assertion forwarded ·
separation check losing the new pairs · exchange INSERT dropping `customer_id` · `CompleteOrder`
clearing it · the cap removed · the cap ignoring an expired assertion · the AbortSignal removed ·
the strict parse loosened.

**Two blind fixtures were caught by mutation-checking rather than by review** — the missing `Cookie`
header, and an assertion fixture whose expiry was in the past (which made the session dead on arrival
once the cap landed, and would have hidden the cap's real behaviour).
